scope: Phase-two third batch: registered resource loading, multi-file/multi-receiver drops, Script loading and object/NMS exports. SDK sources and GPU rendering code unchanged.
status: This batch implemented and validated, including aligned per-item results and retained cleanup diagnostics. Final paired Release comparison and same-program control passed. Phase two remains in progress; completed_phase stays one.
implemented: resource.load, resource.drop, script.load, object.export and script.export use the existing DocumentCommands/DocumentFiles owner and generic operation result table.

Built-in Data Resources, Level Manager, 3D Layout and Schematic entry points submit the same registered commands as the standalone module; window-owned native load/export continuations and raw-ID export buffers were removed.

Copied UTF-8 text arrays extend the version-four C interface without STL or SDK headers. Resource batches own paths, class IDs, receiver/ancestor/scene references and per-item outcomes through duplicate-name questions.

Receivers are checked before each native load and again after input delays. Expired targets and document scopes fail safely; successful items keep the original core undo behavior and partial failures remain visible.

Object options and Behavior Information use the same replaceable registered input view and document.respond. Shared text-field drawing keeps the resource description editor and export form consistent without giving the form native objects or file writing.

Native exports prepare and verify the NMS and optional DSC before publication. NMS publication failure restores a previous DSC or removes a newly created DSC. A restoration failure reports the remaining output and keeps the old description at a recovery path.

Published outputs remain queryable after the requesting view closes or the executor fails after publishing. Per-item created references retain empty slots to align with file names, messages and success flags.
remaining: Phase two: runtime controls, webpage/print operation ownership and outstanding document replacement failure combinations.
NMS/DSC recovery-failure injection remains explicit in F05; Windows/Linux execution was not performed on this macOS host.
Resource-tree browsing, RSC creation/opening and existing DSC editing remain with their view/environment migration. Graph-position import/replacement remains with graph editing.

The original Level_1.NMO was not found in the searched workspace; 15 original-sample suites remain skipped. Generated representative NMO direct-open regressions passed; native desktop acceptance stays separate.
GPU-only timestamps, application allocation counts, preserve-copy/pass/submit counts, native capability queries and retain/release counters are not measured by this harness.

checks.build: macos-arm64 Release: production editor, native tests, UI test executable and independent modules built successfully.

module_ui_inventory.note: Unselected Test Engine cases are not counted as passed.

regressions: Independent module invokes the actual asynchronous resource and object-export commands. Deferred text arrays survive caller buffer destruction.
Four native loads from two files and two receivers preserve four existing Script undo steps. A later file failure retains and reports the earlier success.
Malformed/null text arrays, invalid UTF-8, unknown SDK classes, array-length mismatch and wrong-thread submissions fail before native mutation.
Object identity expiry during the filename dialog and receiver expiry during duplicate choices do not target a same-ID replacement. Document-scope expiry ends duplicate inputs.
Object export success, cancellation and failure after publication preserve the current document, selection, save point and undo history.
NMS/DSC success, existing/new DSC rollback after NMS failure, DSC preparation failure, identical output paths, invalid version response and description cancellation are covered.
The real default export options and Behavior Information controls publish files through the registered file input view; resource loading from an independent module remains undoable.
Independent C/C++ consumers validate the text-array spans without STL or native headers. Native object/NMS export-failure and direct-open/file-byte compatibility regressions passed.
Real directory-permission failure preserves the previous output and reports temporary-file cleanup details through application.operation, rather than only through the view/log.

result_alignment.symptom: A failed second resource item was omitted from the created-reference list, breaking per-item alignment.
result_alignment.fix: Keep an empty created reference for every item that created no object.

sdk.note: --sdk-change permits the previously authorized identity changes already present in both programs; no new SDK work or all-green SDK test run is claimed.

cleanup_diagnostics.symptom: A real POSIX directory-permission failure left a temporary export file; its cleanup diagnostic was logged but absent from the operation result.
cleanup_diagnostics.fix: Export diagnostics include native errors and cleanup/recovery notes, retained with the completed command, including when the export itself succeeded.
cleanup_diagnostics.platform: Directory-permission injection is POSIX-specific; Windows execution remains pending.
